learn.title: Offshore Wind Farms
learn.intro: Offshore wind farms harness wind over oceans, offering vast energy potential with minimal land use. They play a key role in decarbonizing power grids, especially in coastal regions. By converting kinetic energy to electricity, they reduce reliance on fossil fuels and support global climate goals.
learn.c1_text: Offshore turbines are larger and sturdier than land-based ones, designed to withstand harsh marine conditions. For example, the average offshore turbine is 8-10 MW, generating enough power for 20,000 homes annually. Their foundations use floating or fixed platforms, similar to oil rigs but optimized for energy capture.
learn.c2_text: Connecting offshore farms to the grid requires undersea cables, which transmit electricity over long distances. These cables must endure corrosion and storms. A single 600 kV cable can carry power equivalent to 1 GW, enough to supply a city like Mumbai for days.
learn.c3_text: India targets 5 GW offshore wind by 2030, leveraging its 7,500 km coastline. Projects like the Gulf of Cambay pilot aim to replicate successes in Europe. Challenges include financing and technical expertise, but partnerships with IRENA are accelerating progress.
learn.stat1: India: 5 GW offshore wind target by 2030

learn.title: Agrivoltaics
learn.intro: Agrivoltaics combines solar panels with farming, maximizing land use. It provides shade for crops, reduces water usage, and generates clean energy. This dual-purpose approach supports food security and renewable energy targets simultaneously.
learn.c1_text: Solar panels are installed above crops, allowing sunlight to reach plants below. For instance, in the U.S., a 1 MW agrivoltaic system can power 900 homes while growing crops like tomatoes. The panels act as a canopy, protecting against extreme weather.
learn.c2_text: The shade from panels reduces evaporation, cutting irrigation needs by 30-60%. In drought-prone areas, this conserves water while maintaining yields. Studies show lettuce grown under panels has higher sugar content due to controlled light exposure.
learn.c3_text: India's MNRE promotes agrivoltaics in arid regions like Rajasthan. A pilot project in Gujarat combines solar with millet farming, boosting income for farmers. The government offers subsidies to integrate such systems into rural energy plans.

learn.title: Electric Vehicles
learn.intro: Electric vehicles (EVs) use batteries and electric motors to replace gasoline engines. They reduce emissions, lower fuel costs, and improve energy efficiency. With advancements in charging and battery tech, EVs are becoming a cornerstone of sustainable transport.
learn.c1_text: EVs use AC induction or permanent magnet motors, converting battery electricity to motion. A typical EV motor is 90% efficient, far outperforming internal combustion engines. Regenerative braking recovers energy during deceleration, extending range by up to 20% in city driving.
learn.c2_text: Lithium-ion batteries store energy for EVs, with ranges now exceeding 500 km per charge. Charging stations, like those on India's National Highways, use Level 2 (22 kW) or DC fast chargers (150 kW). Battery swapping stations are also emerging in cities like Mumbai.
learn.c3_text: India aims for 30% EV sales by 2030. The Faster Adoption and Manufacturing Initiative (FAMI) subsidizes EVs, while startups like Ather Energy offer affordable models. Public charging infrastructure is expanding, with over 2,000 stations nationwide as of 2024.

learn.title: Solid-State Batteries
learn.intro: Solid-state batteries replace liquid electrolytes with solid materials, offering higher energy density and safety. They charge faster, last longer, and reduce fire risks. This technology could revolutionize EVs and grid storage, enabling longer ranges and safer energy systems.
learn.c1_text: Solid-state batteries eliminate flammable liquids, reducing fire risks. For example, a solid-state cell can withstand punctures without leaking. This makes them ideal for EVs, where safety is critical. They also operate at higher voltages, improving efficiency.
learn.c2_text: These batteries store 2-3x more energy per kg than lithium-ion. A 50 kWh solid-state pack could power an EV for 1,000 km, compared to 500 km with current tech. They charge 10x faster, enabling 80% charge in 15 minutes.
learn.c3_text: India's ISRO and IITs are developing solid-state batteries for EVs. A 2023 pilot project in Bengaluru aims to produce prototypes by 2025. If scaled, this could reduce India's reliance on imported lithium-ion batteries and lower EV costs.

learn.title: Rooftop Solar in India
learn.intro: Rooftop solar panels harness sunlight on buildings, reducing grid dependency. In India, net metering allows homeowners to sell excess power back to the grid. This decentralized approach lowers electricity bills and supports India's renewable energy targets.
learn.c1_text: Rooftop panels convert sunlight to electricity using photovoltaic cells. A 5 kW system in Delhi can generate 6,000 kWh annually, meeting 70% of a household's needs. Panels are angled for maximum sunlight, similar to how solar farms operate but on a smaller scale.
learn.c2_text: Net metering lets users offset bills by exporting surplus power. For instance, if a home produces 10 kWh more than it uses, the grid credits that amount. In India, this reduces monthly costs by up to ₹5,000 for urban households, making solar financially viable.
learn.c3_text: India's MNRE mandates net metering for rooftop solar, with state-level variations. Tamil Nadu has over 1 GW installed, driven by subsidies and feed-in tariffs. The policy has created 100,000+ jobs in solar installation and maintenance since 2020.

learn.title: Electric Buses & Trucks
learn.intro: Electric buses and trucks replace diesel vehicles, cutting emissions and noise pollution. They use dedicated charging infrastructure and offer lower operating costs. Electrifying commercial transport is crucial for achieving urban air quality goals and reducing fossil fuel dependence.
learn.c1_text: Electric buses use onboard chargers or depot charging. A 400 kW fast charger can recharge a bus in 30 minutes. Cities like Delhi have installed 100+ charging stations for buses. Trucks require higher power, with 600 kW chargers enabling 15-minute top-ups.
learn.c2_text: Electric vehicles have 30-50% lower operating costs. A bus saves ₹1.5 lakh annually in fuel and maintenance. For example, Mumbai's electric bus fleet reduces diesel use by 20,000 liters yearly. Trucks benefit from regenerative braking, extending battery life.
learn.c3_text: India plans 10,000 electric buses by 2025 under the FAME II scheme. Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra lead with pilot projects. The government offers subsidies and tax exemptions, while startups like Ola Electric supply buses. This aligns with India's net-zero goals.
learn.stat4: FAME II subsidy: up to ₹15 lakh
